data.title: The poster beside the front door
data.goal: The poster beside the front door
data.situation:
Jo carried a new poster to the front door. It would publicise the open evening and advertise the short film. The team’s target audience included people who had never joined a hall activity, so the poster explained where to enter instead of assuming everyone knew. A local social media influencer had offered to mention the event; Nora sent the same confirmed details used in the printed notice. The resulting publicity brought questions as well as visitors. One reader asked whether the evening was a sales event. Jo added that the film was free to watch and that no purchase was required. Reaching more people meant listening to what they understood, not only counting how many had seen the poster. Visitor: I saw the event on social media. Is there a charge?
Jo: No. The film is free to watch.
Nora: We will make that clearer on the poster.

A local social media influencer had offered to mention the event; Nora sent the same confirmed details used in the printed notice. The resulting publicity brought questions as well as visitors. One reader asked whether the evening was a sales event. Jo added that the film was free to watch and that no purchase was required. readingBlocks.zh: 乔把新海报送到前门。它将宣传开放晚会和短片。目标观众包括从未参加大厅活动的人，所以海报写明入口，没有假定人人都知道。一位本地社交媒体创作者愿意介绍活动，诺拉发给他与印刷通知相同的已确认信息。宣传既带来访客，也带来问题。有读者问是不是促销活动，乔补充短片免费观看、无须购买。让更多人知道，也意味着听听他们理解了什么，而不只是数浏览海报的人。

readingBlocks.en:
Visitor: I saw the event on social media. Is there a charge?
Jo: No. The film is free to watch.
Nora: We will make that clearer on the poster.
readingBlocks.zh:
访客：我在社交媒体上看到了活动，要收费吗？
乔：不用，短片免费。
诺拉：我们会在海报上写得更清楚。
